claim: A Nelson-Narens inspired harness (pre-solve feeling of knowing, post-solve judgment of learning, control policy for trust, retry, aggregate) lifted pooled accuracy of Claude Sonnet-4.6 from 48.3 to 56.9 with no fine-tuning. Authors' claim; equal-token comparison not confirmed in the abstract.
title: LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
transfer: Closest published design to our router: FOK before the attempt, JOL after, rules for trust/retry/aggregate. Replicate with an equal-token best-of-N control before adopting.

claim: Across 20 frontier LLMs and 10,480 evaluations on 524 items in six domains, models fall into three profiles (blanket confidence, blanket withdrawal, selective), and accuracy rank is largely inverted against monitoring-sensitivity rank.
quote: the battery discriminates three profiles consistent with the Nelson-Narens architecture
title: The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
transfer: Do not assume a stronger model monitors better. Measure our model's keep-or-withdraw sensitivity on our own suites before letting it gate anything.

claim: Retrospective monitoring and prospective regulation are dissociable in LLMs: correlation r = .17 with a wide confidence interval (n = 20 models).
title: The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
transfer: Put the control step in program code (rules), not in the model's own decision to withdraw or switch.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (no external feedback) generally fails on reasoning tasks and sometimes lowers performance.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Run revision only when a real check output exists (tests, rule match, retrieved fact). Never run a bare 'reconsider' step.

claim: A critical survey finds no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks exceptionally suited to it. Self-correction works with reliable external feedback, and large-scale fine-tuning enables it.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Strengthens the rule: revision steps need an external signal. It also warns that many positive self-correction results use unfair setups (oracle stop signals).

claim: Counter-evidence: a paper argues LLMs do have intrinsic self-correction when temperature is zero and prompts are unbiased. Single paper, not independent of the debate's framing; treat as contested.
authors: Liu, Nassereldine, Yang, Xu, Hu, Li, Kumar, Lee, Qin, Shi, Xiong
title: Large Language Models have Intrinsic Self-Correction Ability
transfer: If we run any self-revision step, use neutral wording (no 'find the error') and low temperature, and measure it against no-revision.

claim: Multi-turn reinforcement learning (SCoRe) trained self-correction that supervised fine-tuning on offline traces could not. Gains: 15.6% on MATH (Gemini 1.0 Pro) and 9.1% on HumanEval (Gemini 1.5 Flash). Self-correction is described as largely ineffective in untrained modern LLMs.
quote: consistently been found to be largely ineffective in modern LLMs
title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
transfer: We cannot train. So self-correction by prompt alone is not a safe step; keep it behind an external check.

claim: LLM judges recognize their own generations, and self-recognition strength correlates linearly with self-preference after fine-tuning; controlled tests suggest a causal link.
quote: LLMs such as GPT-4 and Llama 2 have non-trivial accuracy at distinguishing themselves from other LLMs and humans.
title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
transfer: Do not let the model pick the best of its own samples by opinion. Use a program check, or have the model derive its expected answer before it sees candidates.

claim: Models can judge the validity of their own claims: larger models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false items (P(True)), and can be trained to predict whether they know the answer (P(IK)). Calibration on new tasks is weaker.
quote: We study whether language models can evaluate the validity of their own claims
title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
transfer: A cheap P(True)-style check on a candidate is usable as a weak signal. Calibrate it per suite; do not trust it out of domain.

claim: Verbalized confidence from black-box LLMs is overconfident. Multi-sample consistency and better aggregation reduce overconfidence. White-box methods are better but the gap is narrow. No method wins everywhere, and all struggle on professional-knowledge tasks.
authors: Xiong, Hu, Lu, Li, Fu, He, Hooi
title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
transfer: Use agreement among independent samples as the 'feeling of rightness' signal, not the model's stated confidence.

claim: Reasoning models are poorly calibrated in token use, especially on easy problems. A training-free black-box decoding method (ThoughtTerminator) improves calibration. DUMB500 is a dataset of very easy problems built to test this.
quote: reasoning models are poorly calibrated, particularly on easy problems
title: THOUGHTTERMINATOR: Benchmarking, Calibrating, and Mitigating Overthinking in Reasoning Models
transfer: Set effort from outside: cap rounds on items where plain attempts already agree; this is our CONVERGE stop rule.

claim: Models write unnecessarily long responses on easy problems but do not extend reasoning enough on hard ones, which suggests they misjudge difficulty. Preference optimization for shorter responses cut length while keeping acceptable accuracy.
title: Between Underthinking and Overthinking: An Empirical Study of Reasoning Length and correctness in LLMs
transfer: Do not let the model's own length habit decide effort. The router sets budget from agreement and checks.

claim: o1-like models spend excessive compute on simple problems with minimal benefit. Authors propose outcome and process efficiency metrics and a self-training fix that reduces compute while preserving accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME.
quote: excessive computational resources are allocated for simple problems with minimal benefit
authors: Chen, Xu, Liang, He, Pang, Yu, Song, Liu, Zhou, Zhang, Wang, Tu, Mi, Yu
title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
transfer: Matches our finding that extra thinking hurts where the first answer is usually right. Supports a stop-early gate.

claim: MetaCrit applies monitoring and control agents (four calls per query) and reports that indiscriminate critique degrades performance, so critique strength should vary by input. Authors claim cost is about one sixth of a dedicated reasoning model of similar accuracy. Multi-agent, no equal-token control confirmed.
quote: Applying the same critique to every input degrades performance.
authors: Hou, Chang, Lu, Qu, Wan, Feng, Hu, Guo
title: Knowing When to Critique: Task-Adaptive Metacognitive Regulation for Reliable LLM Reasoning
transfer: Independent support for our own result: always-doubt hurts single-answer tasks. Make doubt strength depend on the agreement bucket. Note: paraphrased from my fetch summary, quote is a reported paraphrase, verify in the paper.

claim: Models finetuned to predict their own behavior beat a second model trained on the first model's behavior (GPT-4, GPT-4o, Llama-3), which the authors call introspection. It failed on more complex tasks and on out-of-distribution generalization.
quote: unsuccessful on more complex tasks or those requiring out-of-distribution generalization
authors: Binder, Chua, Korbak, Sleight, Hughes, Long, Perez, Turpin, Evans
title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
transfer: Self-prediction works only for simple behavior and needs fine-tuning. Do not expect a prompted model to forecast its own failure on hard items. Use sample agreement instead.

claim: A review in Current Directions in Psychological Science says humans and LLMs can look aligned in metacognition but many differences remain, which matters for human-AI collaboration.
quote: can sometimes appear quite aligned in their metacognitive capacities and behaviors
title: Metacognition and Uncertainty Communication in Humans and Large Language Models
transfer: Human metacognition findings (feeling of rightness, warmth) cannot be copied across by analogy. Each mapped signal needs its own test on the model.

claim: Productive failure meta-analysis: 53 studies, 166 comparisons, problem solving before instruction beat instruction first for conceptual knowledge and transfer. Carried from the earlier brief; I could not open the paper (publisher returned 403), so effect sizes are unchecked.
title: When Problem Solving Followed by Instruction Works: Evidence for Productive Failure
transfer: Only as a design guess: show a stored failure contrast after the first attempt fails, not before. Ordering effect for LLMs is untested.

claim: Testing effect meta-analysis: retrieval practice beats restudy on average g about 0.50, larger with feedback. Carried from the earlier brief; publisher page redirected and I did not open it.
title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: A meta-analytic review of the testing effect
transfer: Human forgetting finding. Does not transfer to context-window memory; only to lesson retrieval design, as a guess.

claim: Self-explanation meta-analysis g = 0.55 over 69 effects from 64 reports; conceptual prompts stronger than generic metacognitive ones. Carried from the earlier brief; Springer page redirected and I did not open it.
title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
transfer: Self-explanation step should ask for the rule behind a failure using real check output, not a generic 'reflect'.

claim: Gap confirmed: in my fetches I found no controlled study applying productive failure, expertise reversal or desirable difficulties to prompting an LLM at equal tokens. Search budget ran out, so this is a gap in my search, not proof of absence.
title: Search coverage note
transfer: Treat expertise-adaptive scaffolding (bare when plain pass rate is high) as our own experiment, with three arms at equal tokens.
